title: A star in the telescope
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Light has a finite travel time. The light arriving now left the star roughly a century ago, so the image carries information about that earlier time.

misconception: A learner may choose: The star exactly as it is now
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Light from a star takes 100 years to reach Earth. When you observe that light, what are you seeing?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Light from a star takes 100 years to reach Earth. When you observe that light, what are you seeing? The star as it was about 100 years ago. Light has a finite travel time. The light arriving now left the star roughly a century ago, so the image carries information about that earlier time.
Visual caption: Light brings an older view. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: Light from a star takes 100 years to reach Earth. When you observe that light, what are you seeing?
options: The star exactly as it is now
The star as it will be in 100 years
The star as it was about 100 years ago
recall.why: Light has a finite travel time. The light arriving now left the star roughly a century ago, so the image carries information about that earlier time.
